title: nsmbtool level-data catalog
description: Every key a module declares in its `level-data`, with the hash the runtime matches on. Written by `nsmbtool glue` from NCPatcher's module dump. A level editor reads this to know what a level may carry beyond the vanilla format: the keys are the schema of the glue block it writes.

levelData.description: Sorted by module, then key. A build allocates nothing here, so the order is for reproducible output and readable diffs only.

key.description: `module.name`, lowercased module id and the key as declared -- `coop.canFly`. This is what the game's code names the key by, and what is hashed.

dataType.description: `flag` is presence alone and carries no payload. `value` is one element. `array` is `arraySize` elements. `sizedArray` is a count followed by that many elements, for a length the level decides.

hash.description: FNV-1a/32 of `key`, as an 8-digit lowercase hex string. THIS IS THE IDENTITY. The runtime finds a key by scanning the level's glue block for this number; the key's spelling exists only to produce it. A published hash must therefore never change, which makes the key name a compatibility surface: renaming a key silently orphans the data every level already stores under the old one.

typeName.description: The C++ type of one element, exactly as the module wrote it. Absent for a flag, which has no payload. An editor cannot size a type from its name alone -- a struct here is opaque -- so a key whose type is not one of the fixed-width primitives is editable only by something that knows the type.
